extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent attorneys/agents), their counsel, and USPTO OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order / settlement agreement resolving a disciplinary proceeding against a registered patent practitioner under the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and the USPTO disciplinary procedures (37 C.F.R. parts 10 and 11). Contains jurisdictional bases, stipulated facts, legal conclusions, sanctions, procedural requirements for reinstatement, publication requirements, and other conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional authority for USPTO disciplinary actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to registered patent agents and attorneys who are subject to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.) and the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement of disciplinary proceedings under 37 C.F.R. § 11.26
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may jointly propose settlement of a disciplinary proceeding without a hearing pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the USPTO Director does not approve the agreement, no reference to the offer of settlement, the contingent acceptance, or stipulations shall be admissible as evidence in any disciplinary proceeding. Settlement agreements may be executed in counterparts and exchanged in PDF; a PDF of an executed signature page will constitute an original executed signature page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of hearing and review rights upon settling
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may waive the right to a hearing under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34–11.57 and the right to seek review under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, provided the USPTO Director agrees to the terms of the settlement agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver is voluntary, with respondent acknowledging competence and that the waiver is not under duress. If Director does not approve, waiver has no effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to cooperate with OED investigations (37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners have a duty to cooperate with the Office of Enrollment and Discipline in investigating allegations of practitioner misconduct; failure to do so violates 37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond to RFIs or other investigative efforts can itself warrant imposition of discipline (e.g., the Order states the failure to cooperate 'warrants the imposition of six months of suspension'). The Official Gazette notice should remind practitioners of this duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public discipline notification standard (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner publicly disciplined on ethical or professional grounds by a state court may be found to have violated 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State court public discipline may be incorporated as grounds for USPTO disciplinary action and affect the length and nature of USPTO sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension on ethical grounds (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Being suspended on ethical grounds by a state court is a circumstance falling within 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such state-imposed suspensions are acknowledged by the respondent and incorporated into USPTO discipline determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposed suspension length and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters for twenty-six (26) months commencing on the date a Final Order approving the Agreement is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent shall remain suspended until the OED Director grants a petition requesting reinstatement; the stipulated suspension length may combine separate components attributable to different misconducts (e.g., six months for failure to cooperate plus state suspensions totaling twenty months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation following reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon reinstatement, respondent shall serve a twenty-four (24) month period of probation beginning on the date the OED Director grants the petition reinstating respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the OED Director believes respondent failed to comply during probation, the Director may issue an Order to Show Cause and seek immediate suspension for up to an additional twenty-four months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for probation enforcement and additional suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director opines respondent failed to comply during probation, the OED Director shall: (1) issue an Order to Show Cause; (2) send it to respondent's last address of record; and (3) grant respondent fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the response period, if OED remains of that opinion, OED shall deliver the Order to Show Cause, respondent's response (if any), and supporting evidence/argument to the USPTO Director and request entry of an order immediately suspending respondent for up to an additional twenty-four (24) months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of review on an imposed suspension during probation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director enters an order suspending respondent during probation and respondent seeks review, such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the USPTO Director's order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appeal or request for review does not stay the suspension ordered by the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations during suspension and OED's duties (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 & 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; the OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These regulatory provisions govern duties and processes related to suspensions and OED obligations (e.g., notification, publication, and procedural steps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a materially consistent notice in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice should state the practitioner's name, registration number, suspension length, probation requirement upon reinstatement, a reminder of the duty to cooperate with OED, a brief explanation of the basis for suspension (e.g., failure to cooperate and state court suspensions), and a citation to the statutory/regulatory authority (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, 11.26, and 11.59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent may not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number, or have his name added to a Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct, in any future disciplinary proceeding (as an aggravating factor and/or to rebut statements), or when considering any request for reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disciplinary record may be used both to aggravate future discipline and to rebut representations by or on behalf of the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition obligations (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall fully comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement requires filing the petition and meeting the regulatory requirements set forth in § 11.60; the OED Director reviews such petitions prior to recommending reinstatement to the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs related to the settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No award of costs between the parties is imposed by the settlement beyond each bearing their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility protections if settlement not approved
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.26, if the USPTO Director does not approve the Agreement, no reference to the offer of settlement, the contingent acceptance thereof, or the fact that the parties stipulated to facts and legal conclusions shall be admissible as evidence in any disciplinary proceeding against respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects the parties' settlement communications in the event the Director declines approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: State court disciplinary conditions as factual/legal grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: State supreme court disciplinary orders (e.g., suspensions with conditions such as restitution, compliance with rule 9.20, MPRE passage) are incorporated as stipulated facts and legal conclusions supporting USPTO discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-imposed conditions (restitution amounts, minimum actual suspension periods, MPRE requirement, compliance with California Rules of Court rule 9.20, and probation conditions) may inform the USPTO's sanction determination and timing for termination of state suspensions; practitioners should be aware that state discipline can trigger USPTO action under the Rules of Professional Conduct.
